writeup.headline: F5 holds a Buy at 65, one point above Hold, on strong quality, cash and momentum despite rich valuation.
writeup.thesis: F5 rates Buy with a composite score of 65, sitting right on the Buy edge, so a small shift in any factor could tip it to Hold. The rating is carried by a debt-free, net-cash balance sheet (score 100), strong momentum (trend 95, shares 42.1 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days) and high quality (84), with an 81.9% gross margin, 29.3% FCF margin and diluted share count down 1.6% year on year. Growth is middling (54), with TTM revenue growth of 9.4% and growth slowed by 0.2 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation is the main drag (27): in absolute terms the multiples are high at 7.9x sales, 26.8x FCF and 30.1x EBIT, with the FCF yield 1.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock is expensive against its own history, more expensive than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S and P/FCF. News is neutral overall (49): a soft FY27 outlook of 8–9% revenue growth and a lower gross-margin range offsets strong AI-related bookings.
key_risks: The FY27 guide of 8–9% revenue growth and a lower gross-margin range disappointed, and the shares reportedly fell about 20% on it, which could erode the trend score that currently supports the rating.
Valuation is high in absolute terms and expensive against its own history, leaving little cushion if growth slows further.
Analysts flag a waning hardware refresh cycle, with Piper Sandler downgrading to Neutral and Needham at Hold.
An existing breach-related class action remains unresolved.
what_would_change: A drop of just 1 point in the composite score would move the rating to Hold; a weaker trend score after the post-guidance sell-off or further negative news could do this.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 15 more points, which would likely require reaccelerating growth or a meaningfully lower valuation.
Delivery on AI-related demand (direct AI bookings of $100M) that lifts growth above the guided 8–9% would support the growth and news scores.
